episodes.discussion_prompt: Use the rehearsal captures to explain why the team chose the photo organizer, which other project it considered, and what evidence would be needed to reconsider; distinguish interface practice from deployment evidence.

concepts.experiment: Compare the photo-organizer mission with another project, then choose mobile and identify the phone app, personal collection, separate training host, and optional remote path.
concepts.evidence: Inspect the mission cards for local-use expectations and different stakeholder obligations; selecting mobile establishes a project, not a proven deployment.
concepts.transfer_question: What different user goal would make another project context preferable?

concepts.experiment: In the labeled practice case, predict a direction, pin a baseline, change the case, capture a contrast, then move the live control again.
concepts.evidence: Compare the original prediction, immutable captures, and current display; the rehearsal demonstrates interface behavior without asserting photo-model performance.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a fresh capture be needed instead of reusing the pinned comparison?

concepts.experiment: Try saving and reading back the rehearsal record, then download its discussion; inspect the stated fallback if browser storage is unavailable.
concepts.evidence: Compare visible session captures, a successfully read-back record, and the downloaded file without treating them as interchangeable or promising unsupported resume.
concepts.transfer_question: When would downloading be preferable to relying on browser storage?

concepts.experiment: Inspect the generated rehearsal discussion and select which saved comparison supports the handoff to the first investigation.
concepts.evidence: Check that project identity, prediction, captured comparison, and the next question remain distinct; a complete practice report contains no claim that the organizer works.
concepts.transfer_question: What would require repeating the rehearsal before using this workflow for a real investigation?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Using saved outcome and execution comparisons, recommend a first intervention for the photo organizer, reject one tempting alternative, and state the new evidence that would reverse the decision.

concepts.experiment: Hold the organizer candidate and runtime fixed while switching a supplied mix of curated photos and personal-photo conditions; reveal labeled outcomes only when available.
concepts.evidence: Inspect input warnings beside matched labeled category outcomes and runtime health; changed inputs alone do not prove harm, and healthy execution does not prove usefulness.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the evidence justify investigating the data rather than buying faster hardware?

concepts.experiment: Compare a supported compute, movement, or overhead intervention against the same photo decode-to-category path, changing one capability at a time.
concepts.evidence: Inspect stage times and the end-to-end bound alongside the unchanged stages; missing cost evidence remains unknown rather than making an upgrade free.
concepts.transfer_question: What change in the dominant stage would make the rejected intervention preferable?

concepts.experiment: Compare supplied task-matched organizer candidates against separate category-quality, response-time, working-memory, and energy requirements.
concepts.evidence: Inspect pass, fail, and unknown gates independently; a fast candidate can remain unusable and an accurate candidate can remain infeasible.
concepts.transfer_question: Which changed requirement would make a currently rejected candidate worth reconsidering?

concepts.experiment: On the separate development host, compare supported changes in training-photo count, work per photo, and realized time per operation while holding the quality target explicit.
concepts.evidence: Inspect execution factors beside supplied learning evidence; reduced training work does not establish that the personal-photo categories remain useful.
concepts.transfer_question: When would collecting or retaining more examples be preferable to the faster training option?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose local, raw-upload, supported filtered, or held placement from the saved comparisons; name the decisive obligation, rejected path, and connection or permission change that would reverse the choice.

concepts.experiment: Keep photo recognition fixed while comparing supported local, raw-upload, and local-filter/remote payload paths under contrasting connection conditions.
concepts.evidence: Inspect decode, preparation, transfer, remote computation, and return work beside the ideal remote-processor bound; link evidence and lower bounds do not certify a real service.
concepts.transfer_question: Under what connection and payload conditions would remote recognition become preferable?

concepts.experiment: Keep the candidate task fixed and compare resource-specific repairs to model residency, decoded-image buffers, and app working state on the phone.
concepts.evidence: Inspect separate capacity gates before timing; reducing package storage or raising arithmetic throughput does not repair an overflowing live buffer.
concepts.transfer_question: What resource change would make a currently nonfitting placement executable?

concepts.experiment: Change a supported indexing policy or operating allowance while retaining an explicit useful-photo-processing requirement.
concepts.evidence: Inspect processed and deferred photos, mission energy, and sustained power separately; deferral saves work by delaying service, while extra energy allowance does not remove a sustained-power limit.
concepts.transfer_question: When would immediate indexing be worth its greater energy or power pressure?

concepts.experiment: Use saved locality, fit, and operating comparisons; change an upload-permission or offline requirement and explicitly select a supported placement or hold.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which paths remain admissible and which filtered paths still need task-retention evidence and compatible interfaces; a placement label alone does not validate them.
concepts.transfer_question: Which permission or availability change would make the rejected placement preferable?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Explain how the new offline requirement changes the organizer using saved dependency and gate evidence; identify one preserved artifact, one rejected repair, and the condition that would reopen the plan.

concepts.experiment: Make new-photo categorization and browsing explicitly offline, then mark revise or preserve on the organizer dependency graph.
concepts.evidence: Inspect the affected requirement, data contract, transform, package, fallback, and validation versions; broad rebuilding has a cost, while a packaging-only change can leave an unsupported claim.
concepts.transfer_question: When would revising the requirement be preferable to rebuilding the affected path?

concepts.experiment: Move discovery of the same offline dependency defect between supplied development stages while keeping repair tasks and resource assumptions fixed.
concepts.evidence: Inspect accumulated rework and elapsed schedule separately alongside the cost of earlier checking; a late discovery does not change the original defect.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the cost of an earlier integration check be justified?

concepts.experiment: Select a supplied evidence bundle, apply a supported local-path repair, and rerun the relevant offline gate on the identified app package.
concepts.evidence: Inspect detected failure, repaired but unverified, missing evidence, and passing evidence separately; a successful conversion does not establish a working offline interaction.
concepts.transfer_question: What missing evidence would make holding the previous app preferable?

concepts.experiment: Replay the same first-use signal and delayed-label timeline, choosing the owner and next evidence request for reports of poor categories.
concepts.evidence: Inspect app health, input changes, selectively reported corrections, and later independent outcomes; referral-only complaints cannot establish population-wide damage.
concepts.transfer_question: When would collecting independent outcomes be preferable to immediately retraining?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Defend the organizer data contract with saved annotation, split, supply, and parity comparisons; reject one misleading shortcut and state what new photo population would require retesting.

concepts.experiment: Allocate a supplied annotation budget between labeling more photos and adjudicating ambiguous category boundaries; compare a changed rubric without altering predictions.
concepts.evidence: Inspect coverage, disagreement, and matched category outcomes under each rubric; broader labels compete with resolving consequential ambiguity, and agreement alone is not truth.
concepts.transfer_question: When would targeted adjudication be preferable to labeling more photos?

concepts.experiment: Compare record-level and event/duplicate-group splits, then contrast train-fitted frozen transforms with fitting before the split or refitting in the app.
concepts.evidence: Inspect shared burst or edited-copy identities and held-out evidence under each split; leaked information can improve the reported score without improving independent behavior.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a stricter grouping boundary be worth a smaller evaluation pool?

concepts.experiment: Hold photo semantics fixed while changing supported storage representation or read, decode, and resize supply relative to the development-host consumer.
concepts.evidence: Inspect file bytes, stage throughput, stalls, and downstream demand; a smaller photo representation can add decoding work and a faster loader can outpace the consumer.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a larger but cheaper-to-decode representation be preferable?

concepts.experiment: Replay a supplied orientation, crop, or normalization mismatch, repair the semantic contract, and trace the affected datasets and category metadata.
concepts.evidence: Inspect keyed transformed values and downstream revalidation requirements beside a drift-only counterexample; legal shapes and an input alert do not establish semantic correctness or harm. Keep validation and quarantine cost beside escaped-error evidence.
concepts.transfer_question: When would quarantine and validation be preferable to accepting a schema-valid batch?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Use the saved shape, dependency, and allocation comparisons to recommend a legal organizer configuration; explain a rejected batch or topology and the resource change that would reverse the choice.

concepts.experiment: Change supported image resolution, network width, or depth and inspect layer shapes; compare a supplied linear-only composition with the required nonlinear mapping.
concepts.evidence: Inspect parameter, operation, and activation allocations beside supplied task evidence; more parameters neither describe every execution cost nor establish useful photo distinctions.
concepts.transfer_question: When would preserving resolution be preferable to increasing model width?

concepts.experiment: On the separate training host, step through a small derivative graph and remove or restore saved forward values needed by a backward rule.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which derivatives remain computable and which values must remain live; a missing dependency yields an invalid backward computation rather than a zero gradient.
concepts.transfer_question: When would keeping an intermediate be preferable to discarding it?

concepts.experiment: Compare training and inference allocation views for the same organizer candidate, then vary supported batch size at fixed optimizer and numerical format.
concepts.evidence: Inspect weights, gradients, optimizer state, and saved activations separately on the development host, and the smaller inference contract on the phone.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a host-side memory problem require a training repair rather than changing the phone package?

concepts.experiment: Grow a supported photo batch while keeping the model and phase fixed, stopping at the declared live-state boundary.
concepts.evidence: Inspect weight traffic per useful photo beside activation memory and capacity failures; reuse gains do not give an executable claim outside the legal budget.
concepts.transfer_question: When would processing fewer photos together be preferable despite poorer weight reuse?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose an organizer architecture from task-matched evidence, explain what the named reference studies teach without treating them as phone measurements, and state when the rejected structure would fit better.

concepts.experiment: Compare supported convolutional and patch-based image candidates and supplied input transformations against the same visual-category requirement.
concepts.evidence: Inspect retained visual distinctions, category outcomes, work, and live state; thumbnail savings can remove the detail needed to distinguish categories.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining more image detail be preferable to the cheaper input?

concepts.experiment: Trace the supported organizer candidates through dense operations, shared local operations, and their memory movement; compare a separately labeled embedding-lookup reference.
concepts.evidence: Inspect arithmetic, weight reuse, input expansion, and resident bytes by operation; the embedding reference demonstrates a cost signature rather than a required photo-organizer component.
concepts.transfer_question: What workload property would make a shared local operation preferable to a dense alternative?

concepts.experiment: Use a named sequence reference to compare materialized and unmaterialized attention scores at fixed history, then inspect prefill and autoregressive decode as separate phases.
concepts.evidence: Inspect score storage, unchanged dense score work, and retained KV state; these reference observations do not describe the non-generative phone-photo workload.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the storage-saving attention implementation be preferable, and what arithmetic would it still leave?

concepts.experiment: In a named embedding-table reference, increase supported table capacity while holding requested rows fixed; retain the organizer decision in a separate task-evidence panel.
concepts.evidence: Inspect resident capacity and per-request accesses separately, including unsupported fit; more IDs or a bigger table do not create evidence for unseen photos or improve the organizer by assumption.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a larger lookup capacity be worth its residency cost in the reference workload?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Recommend an execution policy for the organizer and a separate development policy using saved graph and reuse evidence; reject one unsupported shortcut and name the workload change that reverses the recommendation.

concepts.experiment: Compare eager execution, captured graph regions, and supported fusion for the same organizer operators and image shapes.
concepts.evidence: Inspect launch count and intermediate traffic separately beside required graph outputs; fusion does not establish that arithmetic or differentiation dependencies disappeared.
concepts.transfer_question: When would easier inspection in eager execution be preferable to a captured plan?

concepts.experiment: Change the supported reuse horizon and frequency of image-shape signatures, comparing installed-app indexing with explicitly separate development experiments.
concepts.evidence: Inspect setup, recompilation, graph breaks, and repeated execution over each actual horizon; a faster invocation may still lose over a short or changing session.
concepts.transfer_question: When would signature churn make an eager policy preferable?

concepts.experiment: On the development host, revisit the small derivative graph from Lab 05 and compare supported saved-value and recomputation policies.
concepts.evidence: Inspect reverse dependencies, live saved state, and repeated work; automatic differentiation preserves a contract and recomputation spends execution to reduce retained state.
concepts.transfer_question: When would recomputation be preferable to retaining all forward values?

concepts.experiment: Compare native phone support, explicit fallback partitions, and rejected export for the same organizer graph and shapes.
concepts.evidence: Inspect operation support, transfer boundaries, fallback cost, and required preprocessing/postprocessing; dropping a required stage changes the task rather than fixing export.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a simpler fully supported candidate be preferable to a partitioned one?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose a host training recipe from saved memory, progress, and profile evidence; explain a rejected faster-looking recipe and the change that would make it preferable, without claiming the phone artifact is validated.

concepts.experiment: On the separate development host, compare full training with supported restricted adaptation for the same organizer dataset and target.
concepts.evidence: Inspect weights, gradients, optimizer state, and activations separately; frozen weights can reduce update state while leaving forward state or backward dependencies.
concepts.transfer_question: When would broader adaptation justify its additional training state?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported resident, micro-batch/accumulated, and checkpointed training recipes at a matched effective batch where equivalence is supported.
concepts.evidence: Inspect legal capacity, repeated computation, and update semantics; a matching batch label alone does not establish the same recipe or quality.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a slower checkpointed recipe be preferable to reducing the effective batch?

concepts.experiment: Reveal supplied matched progress observations for supported numerical recipes rather than deriving category quality from the step-time control.
concepts.evidence: Inspect step time and arrival at the declared photo-quality target separately, retaining failed or unavailable target outcomes and preparation costs.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the slower numerical recipe reach useful quality more defensibly?

concepts.experiment: Inspect a partially revealed host profile, try an ineffective capability increase, then compare a supported repair to its binding preparation, movement, or compute stage.
concepts.evidence: Inspect useful progress, stalls, realized operation time, and changed bottlenecks; a busy accelerator alone does not establish efficient learning.
concepts.transfer_question: What new profile evidence would make the initially ineffective intervention preferable?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Recommend a photo-selection policy against the full-data baseline using saved learning, coverage, and campaign evidence; identify a rejected shortcut and when reuse or population change would reverse the choice.

concepts.experiment: Choose among supported photo-allocation pilots and reveal work-matched learning observations on the same independent evaluation population.
concepts.evidence: Inspect progress toward the final category-quality obligation beside work spent; a favorable early gain or smaller subset does not establish reaching the target.
concepts.transfer_question: When would retaining the full collection be preferable to the promising subset?

concepts.experiment: Allocate a finite subset among common scenes, low-light cases, unusual compositions, and less common categories under supplied coverage floors.
concepts.evidence: Inspect counts, eligibility, task evidence, and infeasible allocations separately; meeting coverage counts is necessary evidence, not guaranteed adequate outcomes.
concepts.transfer_question: When would preserving difficult photos be preferable to selecting only apparently clean examples?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported selection/scoring campaigns over different reuse horizons while requiring matched accepted organizer quality.
concepts.evidence: Inspect scorer preparation, source reads, selection, subset training, and refresh costs; changed photo populations or targets can invalidate reuse.
concepts.transfer_question: How much valid reuse would make the selection campaign preferable to full-data training?

concepts.experiment: Keep selected photo identities fixed and compare supported stream/discard, scattered reads, and materialized subset layouts.
concepts.evidence: Inspect bytes read, decode work, host stalls, repacking time, and extra storage; saved training examples need not produce saved source reads.
concepts.transfer_question: When would repacking the chosen photos be preferable to reading them in place?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Select one exact deployable organizer bundle using saved resource and quality comparisons; reject a smaller-looking artifact, identify missing evidence, and state the condition that would reverse the selection.

concepts.experiment: Change a supported organizer representation while retaining separate package bytes, weights, decoded-photo buffers, and app/runtime working allocations.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which allocation actually violates the shared-phone reservation; smaller storage can leave the binding activation or image buffer unchanged.
concepts.transfer_question: When would lowering input or buffer demand be preferable to compressing weights?

concepts.experiment: Compare supplied post-training and training-aware numerical candidates using matched calibration photos and independent category evidence.
concepts.evidence: Inspect per-category outcomes, resource gates, preparation cost, and unavailable quality results; technique names do not guarantee recovery of lost distinctions.
concepts.transfer_question: When would training-aware preparation be worth its additional cost?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported dense, masked, indexed, structurally smaller, and precision-specific execution paths on the intended phone runtime.
concepts.evidence: Inspect metadata, conversion, actual operation support, traffic, and execution evidence; zeros or fewer stored bits do not establish faster supported kernels.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a larger dense package be preferable to a sparse one?

concepts.experiment: Compare exact ordered transformation bundles against their single-transform candidates under the same app workload and quality gates.
concepts.evidence: Inspect joint resource consumption, supported conversion paths, and matched task outcomes, keeping missing composite evidence unknown; independent reductions do not certify the combination.
concepts.transfer_question: When would keeping a single transformation be preferable to the combined artifact?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Recommend a legal phone execution intervention from saved mapping and whole-path evidence; explain the rejected peak-performance argument and the workload change that would make it relevant.

concepts.experiment: For a supported organizer operator, compare arithmetic, bandwidth, and legal reuse interventions at the identified phone interface.
concepts.evidence: Inspect the relevant resource ceiling and intensity alongside operation support; a peak at another interface or unsupported precision cannot improve this workload by assumption.
concepts.transfer_question: When would greater arithmetic capability become preferable to reducing movement?

concepts.experiment: Step through supported stationary schedules for the same image operator, choosing which weights, activations, or partial sums remain resident.
concepts.evidence: Inspect counted traffic at each boundary and its sourced energy consequences; reducing one traffic category can increase another.
concepts.transfer_question: What shape or capacity change would make another operand worth keeping resident?

concepts.experiment: Grow a supported tile until live buffers or accumulators fail, then compare a legal smaller tile and an aligned or off-grid image shape.
concepts.evidence: Inspect reuse, buffer occupancy, fringe work, and legal execution status; an illegal tile has no valid runtime rather than an invented spill result. Account for the declared accumulator width separately from narrow operands.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a smaller tile be preferable even though it offers less reuse?

concepts.experiment: Carry the selected legal kernel intervention through phone decode, resize, transfers, fallback operators, and category-metadata update.
concepts.evidence: Inspect changed kernel time beside untouched app stages and end-to-end response; a kernel win can be capped by work outside the accelerator.
concepts.transfer_question: When would improving decode or fallback be preferable to further kernel tuning?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Write one bounded organizer performance claim from saved matched protocols and outcome evidence; reject an attractive unsupported claim and name the additional condition that would require retesting.

concepts.experiment: Compare a proposed warm model-only claim with a supported photo-to-visible-category timer, then repair endpoints and stage inclusion before rerunning.
concepts.evidence: Inspect exact artifact, input mix, cold/warm state, and included work; similarly named models do not make unlike timer boundaries comparable.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a model-only measurement be preferable for diagnosis while remaining insufficient for an app claim?

concepts.experiment: Allocate the supplied measurement budget between more requests within a run and independent paired runs, retaining randomized comparison order where supported.
concepts.evidence: Inspect within-run and between-run variation alongside the minimum useful app improvement; correlated requests cannot substitute for independent evidence.
concepts.transfer_question: When would more independent runs be preferable to extending one run?

concepts.experiment: Replay supported idle, contended, cold-start, and sustained-indexing conditions for the same organizer claim.
concepts.evidence: Inspect foreground tails, delayed categories, and complete-window energy beside average execution; favorable short idle behavior supports only that narrow envelope.
concepts.transfer_question: When would restricting background indexing be preferable to accepting the faster idle configuration?

concepts.experiment: Set category and slice obligations before revealing paired supplied photo outcomes and calibration; test a supported calibration repair.
concepts.evidence: Inspect per-condition coverage, classifications, and confidence separately; calibration can change without repairing wrong categories and untested photos remain untested.
concepts.transfer_question: When would new evaluation photos be preferable to tuning the confidence mapping?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Choose an organizer service policy from saved identical-trace comparisons; report foreground behavior and uncategorized or deferred photos together, reject one misleading latency win, and give a reversal trigger.

concepts.experiment: Compare supported decode/host and model interventions on the same import-to-visible-category path, including foreground access to the organizer.
concepts.evidence: Inspect complete path stages, waiting, and transferred work; faster inference can leave the interaction unchanged when decode or metadata work dominates.
concepts.transfer_question: When would host-path improvement be preferable to another inference optimization?

concepts.experiment: Replay identical photo arrivals at fixed admission under two supported local service-capacity cases. Compare headroom, then test deferral or bounded admission as a separate policy.
concepts.evidence: Inspect utilization, backlog, and foreground/background waiting on the same photo trace as service capacity changes. Count deferred or rejected useful work separately from completed-photo latency.
concepts.transfer_question: When would accepting a longer indexing backlog be preferable to admitting all work immediately?

concepts.experiment: Compare immediate dispatch with supported size-or-timeout photo batches under identical arrivals and foreground requirements.
concepts.evidence: Inspect batch formation delay, realized group sizes, actual executed work, and late categories; a longer window can add waiting without producing reuse.
concepts.transfer_question: When would immediate dispatch be preferable despite a lower maximum throughput?

concepts.experiment: Increase supported in-flight decoded photos and concurrent work until app memory fails, then compare legal reservations; inspect any KV-cache example only as a named generative reference. In the separately labeled Language-serving reference, compare prefill/decode demands and a supported KV-limited concurrency change.
concepts.evidence: Inspect native image buffers, model residency, app state, and service losses separately; photo buffers are not a KV cache and unrelated language state does not determine organizer capacity. Keep first-token delay, active-stream cadence, and KV residency separate from native task state.
concepts.transfer_question: When would limiting concurrency be preferable to a smaller model package?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Recommend an incident response and safe transition using saved keyed replay and recovery evidence; reject an inadequate rollback, preserve unresolved outcomes, and state what later evidence could change the response.

concepts.experiment: Choose a monitor and replay early resource/input signals followed by delayed independent category or retrieval outcomes after the app update.
concepts.evidence: Inspect alert sensitivity, evidence maturity, confirmation cost, and owner response; a change in crop or orientation signals investigation before it establishes user harm.
concepts.transfer_question: When would targeted confirmation be preferable to immediate retraining?

concepts.experiment: Compare request-keyed decoded and transformed values for the same original photos across immutable releases, then repair a supplied orientation or crop mismatch.
concepts.evidence: Inspect per-photo parity, fitted state, transform/model/runtime identity, and category-index lineage; similar aggregate distributions can conceal mismatched values.
concepts.transfer_question: When would repairing preprocessing be preferable to replacing weights?

concepts.experiment: Change shadow or canary exposure while retaining complete baseline and candidate app reservations; compare supported staged deployment and hold.
concepts.evidence: Inspect copy residency, buffers, execution overlap, and evidence strength separately; little traffic does not imply little resident memory.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a staged or paused rollout be preferable to a small-exposure concurrent canary?

concepts.experiment: Try a supplied weights-only rollback, then restore a compatible decoder/transform/model/category-index bundle; contrast a separate population-shift incident.
concepts.evidence: Inspect replayed outputs and state compatibility after containment; stale metadata can survive rollback, while a new photo population can invalidate both model versions.
concepts.transfer_question: When would collecting new population evidence be preferable to rolling back again?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Defend permitted organizer use or a hold using saved intended-outcome, affected-population, feedback, and lifecycle evidence; explain a rejected mitigation and what independent evidence would reverse the recommendation.

concepts.experiment: State useful retrieval goals for declared user populations. On the same supplied audited photo outcomes with different category prevalence, compare predicted-category parity with equal opportunity for finding relevant photos; justify the criterion.
concepts.evidence: Inspect user-group counts, base rates, proxy versus retrieval outcomes, and criterion-dependent pass/fail/insufficient gates with predictions fixed. Photo-condition robustness alone does not establish fairness toward users.
concepts.transfer_question: When would changing the justified criterion alter the release verdict without changing the model?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported organizer mitigations on matched supplied cases while keeping error consequences, retrieval/category obligations, and app resource gates separate.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which obligations improve or fail alongside preparation and operating costs; no scalar fairness score or invented accuracy tradeoff resolves the policy choice.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a costlier mitigation be preferable to retaining the aggregate winner?

concepts.experiment: Compare user-correction-only learning evidence with a supplied independent photo-audit policy and a supported cause-specific response.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which photos were surfaced, reviewed, corrected, or independently checked; selective corrections can leave unseen or confidently miscategorized photos invisible while audits consume effort.
concepts.transfer_question: When would independent auditing be preferable to treating more corrections as representative feedback?

concepts.experiment: Compare supported lifecycle alternatives at equal useful retrieval service across separate host preparation, app operation, and any permitted remote path.
concepts.evidence: Inspect dollars, energy, emissions, data-handling exclusions, and accounting coverage separately; fewer phone inference operations alone do not establish a lower whole-service footprint.
concepts.transfer_question: When would additional preparation cost be justified by the supported operating horizon?

episodes.discussion_prompt: Defend release, restriction, baseline retention, fallback, or hold for one exact organizer configuration using compatible saved evidence; identify the rejected alternative, unresolved obligation, and next change that reverses the decision.

concepts.experiment: Audit the proposed release dossier by requirement, photo population, split, transforms, model/package, runtime, protocol, and background-policy identity; replay or reject supplied incompatible links.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which prior claims actually support this app configuration, retaining missing records as unknown rather than inheriting a pass from project identity or completion.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a narrower coherent dossier be preferable to the larger mixed packet?

concepts.experiment: Carry one supported earlier candidate change through the existing complete app path and joint quality, resource, and useful-service gates.
concepts.evidence: Inspect compatible saved or replayed comparisons with the rejected alternative under the same contract; a compression or kernel win may lose its advantage in foreground use.
concepts.transfer_question: When would the simpler baseline be preferable to the locally faster candidate?

concepts.experiment: Tighten a supported shared-memory allowance, foreground requirement, offline obligation, or photo-import demand for the same identified candidate.
concepts.evidence: Inspect unchanged original consumption beside newly failed acceptance gates and supported repair, restriction, or hold options; changing a policy limit does not rewrite the measurement.
concepts.transfer_question: Which smallest supported requirement change would reverse the release recommendation?

concepts.experiment: Apply a supported crop-path update or photo-population change and use familiar parity, outcome, and service instruments to choose a cause-specific response.
concepts.evidence: Inspect which earlier evidence expires and which physical or behavioral claims remain supported; restored execution does not establish restored useful categories.
concepts.transfer_question: When would a new data investigation be preferable to restoring the previous app bundle?

provenance.numerical_status: Intended experiments; matched numerical fixtures and observed outcome evidence require separate implementation and validation.
